en: Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa. Oṃ. Of this mantra of the Śrī Saṅkaṣṭaharaṇa Stotra, the deity is Śrī Mahāgaṇapati; its application is in recitation (japa) for the purpose of removing distress.

Oṃ Oṃ Oṃ! That supreme nature which is the form of the syllable *oṃ*, which for three days manifests as the fourth state (*turīya*) beyond the three qualities (*traiguṇya*), and which the lords of yogis perceive through the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*) as a form of vermilion light endowed with all attributes— may that [form] unite with the illustrious Lord Hara.
They meditate upon Gaṇeśa, the elephant-faced one, who pervades everywhere—gaṃ gaṃ gaṃ gaṃ gaṃ. || 1 ||
*Vaṃ vaṃ vaṃ*, she worships Vighnarāja with her right hand placed upon his trunk;
*kraṃ kraṃ kraṃ*, she crushes the enemy forces with the gesture of wrath at the foot of the Kalpa tree;
*daṃ daṃ daṃ*, she bears a single tusk like the face of a sage, worthy of being served by the wish-fulfilling cow.
Dhaṃ dhaṃ dhaṃ, saluting him who supports [the world], who possesses wealth and supreme intellect, and who has Siddhi and Buddhi as his two companions. || 2 ||
Tuṃ tuṃ tuṃ! To You of lofty form, who have gone upon the path of the sky pervading the ends of the quarters;
Klīṃ klīṃ klīṃ! O Lord of Kāma, whose swarm of intoxicated bees is agitated by the flowing ichor;
Hrīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ! O You tawny-hued by the syllable Hrīṃ, whose head and trunk are meditated upon by all the best of sages.
Śrīṃ Śrīṃ Śrīṃ Śrīṃ! I bow to the form of Heramba, who is the refuge of the entire multitude of treasures. || 3 ||
Lauṃ, Lauṃ, Lauṃ—the syllable preceded by *kāra*, like the *praṇava* among the strings of mantra-pearls;
the pure seed-syllable of Vighneśa, resembling the moon’s rays, attainable through the meditation of yogis;
Ḍaṃ, Ḍaṃ, Ḍaṃ—having the form of a ḍāma, which shatters the fear of worldly existence and shines with the brilliance of ten million suns.
Whichever Lord of Sacrifice the best of sages recites, whether external or internal.

Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ! [I meditate upon] the golden-colored one, whose qualities are enumerated in the Vedas, the compassionate Śūrpakarṇa, who is to be meditated upon as the orb of the sun, shining upon his chest with a serpent as a sacred thread (yajñopavīta);
he is served by sprouts accompanied by the syllables iṣṭha-ṭha-ṭha-ṭha, ending with svāhā, hūṃ, phaṭ, and namaḥ.
I take refuge in the Lord, the foundation of the greatness of the mantras multiplied sevenfold by ten million. || 5 ||
First is the triangular seat (pīṭha), above which is a beautiful and pure six-petaled lotus;
above that, a pure line, or an eight-petaled lotus, or a square of one's own radiance.
In the center is the seed-syllable *huṃ*, followed by the six limbs of the Blessed One upon the six corners.
The eight Śaktis, the Siddhis, Bahula-Gaṇapati, Viṣṭara, and the group of eight.

The eight [deities] beginning with Dharma are well-known and renowned throughout the ten directions as a multitude of banners; [there is] the skull-bowl, the Lord of the Field (Kṣetrapati), the entire lineage of Sages, and the Great Lord of Mantras and Mudrās.

He who, endowed with devotion, thus mutters the name of Gaṇapati while offering flowers, incense, unbroken rice, food offerings such as sweetmeats (*modaka*), along with hymns of praise and the resounding noise of radiant songs and musical instruments—[he attains success]. || 7 ||

Kings serve him like his servants, and the assembly of young women always attends him like maidservants; Fortune, endowed with all her limbs, dwells in his home, and all the worlds are his attendants.
His sons and daughters are pure, he is victorious on the field of battle, and he is a hero even in the game of dice.
In the heart of that fortunate one who possesses devotion, Rudra dwells as the Lord Vighnarāja.
Thus ends the "Eight Verses on Gaṇeśa for the Removal of Distress."
